cause: The model had a severe "B bias"—it chose answer B 61% of the time regardless of correctness. The main culprit was layer 14's MLP, which at the answer position pushed logits strongly toward B (+5.9) and away from A, C, D. A rank-1 edit on layer 14's down-projection (scaled to k=5) cut that B-push and lifted overall clinical accuracy from 66% to 75%, with clear gains in contraindication and diagnosis questions and a modest improvement in dosing. Further edits to layer 22's linear attention degraded performance on general knowledge, so they were rolled back. The remaining failures (e.g., serotonin syndrome with linezolid/SSRI, metformin contraindication at eGFR<30, loperamide in bloody diarrhea) are specific knowledge gaps that a single directional edit cannot fix.
